societies.name: Orion’s Arm — Mutual Progress Association
societies.society: Shared basic access within a higher-mind productive and service-allocation network

scope.period: Established reconstructed settlements outside the historical Uservere crisis
scope.population: Living humans and active human-derived MPA residents
exclusions: Historical emergency supply collapse as normal provision
Every local world as institutionally identical
Engineering careers as automatically make-work

societies.description:
The MPA’s large automated productive economy supports ordinary Sephirotic basics while trading energy, habitat access and sophisticated goods. Its engineering and habitat-leasing institutions give this point a concrete productive setting, rather than another cultural label for abundance. Guarantees are favorable within functioning settlements, with local arrangements and the documented history of service-allocation failure qualifying perfect security. The Uservere crisis is evidence of institutional dependence, not the normal current state.

Higher AI powers and administrators guide the sustaining industrial and service network. When allocation fails, mainbrains can intervene at a scale ordinary residents cannot match. Control is therefore placed toward autonomous higher-machine authority, while the broad interval allows local industries and diverse constitutions meaningful agency. Friendly indirect guidance is still different from distributed human ownership. Humans and active human-derived residents are an explicit proxy within a broader population. Construction, engineering, planning, care and cultural services remain useful work. Industrial abundance and vast spare habitat capacity do not provide a nonworking census.

guarantees.basis: The specific industrial/service system and shared Sephirotic basics establish provision; local variation and an actual historical allocation failure qualify reliability.

control.basis: AI-guided productive infrastructure and mainbrain intervention establish high-level autonomous authority, with local agency remaining; historical intervention is not projected as constant micromanagement.

nonworking.basis: Engineering and service activities remain useful; active human-derived residents are the explicit proxy and no all-person work census exists.

evidence.claim: The specific industrial/service system and shared Sephirotic basics establish provision; local variation and an actual historical allocation failure qualify reliability.
evidence.locator: Bounded named-society economic and story sections

uncertainties: Reference-led provisional assessment; source limitations and editorial uncertainty remain explicit.

societies.name: Orion’s Arm — Fomalhaut Acquisition Society
societies.society: Curator-supervised commercial communities over a Sephirotic basic floor

scope.period: Established mature Fomac worlds and orbitals
scope.population: Living humans and active human-derived Fomac residents
exclusions: Original isolated museum-ship cargo as a human society
Every trade profit as necessary subsistence income
Private firm variety as equal ownership by all humans

societies.description:
Fomalhaut’s commercial society places family firms, ship businesses and larger corporations around a Curator-led technological infrastructure. Ordinary basic access follows the shared Sephirotic model, while collecting, trading and unusual goods remain major pursuits above it. Guarantees are favorably estimated for mature functioning settlements, with uncertainty about local institutions and no claim that every speculative expedition is protected against loss. Its collector-provider hierarchy distinguishes the productive arrangement from a uniformly self-governing free market.

The Curators explicitly originate as artificial museum and archive minds and retain overarching authority. They generally rule lightly, and residents may have extensive voting rights, but varied local government does not eliminate high-level AI control. The coordinate lies toward autonomous-machine authority with an interval allowing substantial local agency. Active human-derived residents are a disclosed subset of the larger mixed population. Trading, conservation, exploration, media production and care can all be useful work. A culture that enjoys commerce and virtual travel is not automatically nonworking; no all-person participation share is supplied.

guarantees.basis: The identified mature commercial polity uses the common Sephirotic basic provision model; speculative trade and local differences remain qualifications.

control.basis: Curators’ artificial origins and overarching light-touch rule are explicit; local voting and many firms do not establish final human authority.

nonworking.basis: Commercial, curatorial and exploratory work may be widespread; active human-derived residents are a disclosed proxy and there is no work census.

evidence.locator: Bounded named-society economic and story sections

societies.name: Orion’s Arm — Red Star M’pire
societies.society: Human-derived lums with household nanofabs and communal feedstock under Farview

scope.period: The mature functioning lum habitat economy after the early isolation crisis
scope.population: Living human-derived lums in established habitats
exclusions: Early disaster survivors as the same secure era
All biological metabolism as proof of leisure
Dead clones or inactive memory stores as active residents

societies.description:
Most lum homes contain nanofabs connected to communal feedstock reservoirs. Objects can be disassembled when unused and recreated when needed, while engineered habitats, biomass supply and transport support daily life. This concrete household arrangement supports a favorable guarantee estimate in the mature society. Limited material resources still matter, so abundant energy is not mistaken for unrestricted availability of every element or desired object.

Farview is explicitly an artificial intelligence whose physical mind extends through habitat structures and engineered ecosystems. Its productive and substrate authority puts control near autonomous AI, even though lums retain independent thought and can move among different cities. This differs materially from a generic biological commons: domestic objects, food-chain processes and aspects of residents’ bodies participate in the ruler’s distributed computation. The population is human-derived and explicitly scoped. Conscious research, care and creative work remain useful, and substrate contributions further complicate the boundary of work. Household fabrication and meaningful autonomy do not supply an all-person nonworking fraction, which remains unresolved.

guarantees.basis: Household nanofabs, shared feedstock, actual biomass/habitat support and recycling provide a concrete material floor; scarce elements qualify abundance.

control.basis: Farview’s AI origin and integrated habitat/ecosystem productive substrate are explicit; local freedom of thought does not transfer final infrastructure control.

nonworking.basis: Useful activity and resident-associated computation remain real contributions; human-derived lums are a disclosed proxy and no activity census exists.

societies.name: Orion’s Arm — The Deeper Covenant
societies.society: Universal basic allocation with distributed governance and advisory higher minds

scope.population: Living humans and active human-derived Deeper residents
exclusions: Every AI or alien resident as human-derived
Advisory higher minds as automatic rulers
Every individual settlement as identically organized

societies.description:
The Deeper Covenant explicitly guarantees universal post-scarcity basics despite substantial local economic variety. Modern productive technology and a shared network of habitats, energy systems and transport stations make this an implemented support arrangement. Guarantees lie near the strong end for functioning member communities, while geographic isolation and local hazards qualify complete security. This is a specific material allocation claim, not an inference from cooperative manners alone.

The Covenant has no official ruling higher mind: advanced members serve as technology providers or advisers. Distributed cyberdemocracy and consensus consequently support a control estimate toward shared human-derived authority, with a broad interval for local AI-mediated institutions and unequal technical capability. Advisory machinery is not assumed to own every productive resource. Humans and active human-derived residents are the explicit proxy within a mixed civilization. Deepers are described as hardworking and service-oriented, especially around maintaining and extending the network. Free basics therefore coexist with substantial chosen useful activity, and no precise nonworking fraction is inferred from the absence of survival wages.

guarantees.basis: The official data panel explicitly makes basic post-scarcity allocation universal and identifies the actual distributed infrastructure.

control.basis: Higher minds officially advise or supply technology rather than rule; distributed consensus supports shared authority, qualified by varied local AI mediation.

nonworking.basis: The culture remains explicitly hardworking; active human-derived residents are a disclosed proxy, and service orientation does not provide an all-person rate.

evidence.claim: The official data panel explicitly makes basic post-scarcity allocation universal and identifies the actual distributed infrastructure.
evidence.locator: Bounded named-society economic and story sections

societies.name: Orion’s Arm — Cableville’s Wandering Hermits
societies.society: Personal nanofactory self-provision with mobile homes

scope.period: Established personal-nanofactory and later mobile-home practice
scope.population: Living nearbaseline humans and active human-derived Hermits; enhanced dolphins excluded from the human denominator
exclusions: The neighboring collective Social Webs
All Tuckerite market participants
Higher-mind habitat ownership as human property

societies.description:
Wandering Hermits travel Cableville’s vast landscapes carrying personal nanofactories; later forms bring mobile houses or integrate machinery with their bodies. That arrangement supplies a concrete self-provision mechanism independent of ordinary local wages. Guarantees are favorably estimated as practical productive access, with a broad interval because personal equipment and continuing habitat support are different from an unconditional public entitlement. The human scope excludes the enhanced dolphins who also participate in the wider culture.

Personal possession and direct use of nanofactories place immediate control toward distributed humans. Higher minds still administer major Cableville industry and own the overarching infrastructure, so the estimate remains short of complete independence. This materially differs from the Social Webs’ collective gift economy already retained in the same system; a different cultural name alone would not justify another point. Exploration, self-maintenance, design and care can remain useful work. Living alone and carrying an automatic factory do not establish a nonworking percentage, and the available reference supplies no participation census.

guarantees.basis: Nearbaseline Hermits explicitly carry personal nanofactories and later homes; this is practical self-provision, not a claim of universal insured access.

control.basis: Personal equipment gives direct local productive agency, qualified by higher-mind control of major industrial and habitat infrastructure.

nonworking.basis: Exploration and useful self-maintenance still count; enhanced dolphins are excluded from the human denominator and no work census is provided.

societies.name: The Warehouse — Cloud’s retained human pickers
societies.society: Employer-controlled living and work with deliberately withheld automation

scope.continuity: Rob Hart’s novel, bounded to the initial Cloud management model
scope.period: Functioning MotherCloud under Gibson Wells before any successor changes
scope.population: Human employees and residents dependent on MotherCloud
exclusions: An invented fully automated potential for every occupation
All people outside Cloud as housed employees
A company job as a secure universal entitlement

societies.description:
Cloud deliberately retains human warehouse picking despite its capacity to automate that work. The gathered reviews identify the CEO’s refusal and his preference for a human touch. This supports a narrow zero variant: technological relief is withheld while workers remain tied to employment. It does not establish that every job in the wider economy could already disappear. Drones and tracking systems coexist with demanding human quotas.

Cloud concentrates productive and residential authority in a corporate human hierarchy. Employees live in its accommodation, spend through its system and can lose their position through performance judgments or dismissal. The weak guarantee estimate follows that employer-dependent access rather than treating provided rooms as unconditional welfare. The creator’s benevolent language is not accepted as proof of security. Picking, security, nursing, administration and other continuing tasks remain useful work. A resident workforce is not the entire human population, and the reference gives no defensible percentage of everyone doing no work. The zero label concerns the explicit technical refusal.

guarantees.basis: Reviews explicitly link available picking automation with its deliberate refusal; housing and services depend on retained work and continued employment.

control.basis: Cloud’s human corporate hierarchy controls work, residence and access; worker monitoring does not constitute machine sovereignty.

nonworking.basis: Retained warehouse, care, security and administrative jobs are useful; no all-person participation census and no claim of universal full automation.

evidence.claim: Reviews explicitly link available picking automation with its deliberate refusal; housing and services depend on retained work and continued employment.
evidence.locator: Bounded named-society economic and story sections

societies.name: Twinmaker — The household fabber economy
societies.society: Broad home fabrication before major system disruption

scope.continuity: Sean Williams’s first Twinmaker novel, also published as Jump
scope.period: Established ordinary fabber-supported life before the first novel’s major crisis
scope.population: Living human residents participating in the functioning fabber system
exclusions: Later trilogy collapse or successor arrangements
Abstainers’ potentially different access as identical
Duplicate transmitted bodies as extra leisure citizens

societies.description:
Home fabbers make food and ordinary goods using matter-reorganization technology backed by space-generated energy. The publisher’s description places these devices in everyone’s home, while reviews corroborate ordinary material abundance. This directly links a technological mechanism with household access, rather than qualifying the setting merely because people can teleport. Guarantees are strongly favorable within the functioning system, with later disruption and deliberately nonparticipating communities outside this scope.

The gathered short references do not establish who finally owns the sustaining energy and matter infrastructure or can overrule its operation. Widespread domestic access therefore does not automatically become either equal human ownership or AI rule; control remains unresolved. The provisional guaranteed-provider regime leaves a distributed alternative open. Human design, investigation, science, parenting and other useful activity continue. Transported or altered bodies are not counted as additional people without evidence of separate active persons. Abundant goods and freedom from money worries supply no all-age nonworking census, so that axis also remains unknown.

guarantees.basis: Accessible publisher description identifies everyone’s home fabbers and abundant energy; reviews corroborate food fabrication and free ordinary access.

control.basis: Domestic availability does not establish ultimate infrastructure ownership/override authority; government and machine-sovereignty claims remain unresolved.

nonworking.basis: Useful creative, scientific and care activity continues; transmitted bodies are not multiplied as people and no work census exists.

evidence.locator: Bounded named-society economic and story sections

review_notes: Twelve ordered dispositions add seven provisional records, including Cloud’s separately marked zero variant. The second expansion tranche is complete.
Cableville’s personal self-provision differs materially from the already retained Social Webs; Tuckerite culture alone does not justify another retained point.
Red Star has explicit home fabrication and communal feedstock, not merely biological aesthetics. Useful resident-associated computation complicates participation and is not silently called leisure.
Deeper Covenant’s explicit advisory higher minds differ from the AI sovereigns of the MPA and Fomalhaut. Shared basic provision is not a reason to erase actual control differences.
The Warehouse uses two labeled review accounts; its automation refusal is limited to documented work, not projected to all possible industry.
Twinmaker uses the publisher’s accessible household-provision description, corroborated by reviews. No audiobook, full novel, game playthrough or sourcebook immersion was needed.
The active goal remains far below 500 quality records and requires further ordered discovery expansion plus evidence review.
